Subject: Clarify billing for long context + rounding behavior

Hi Avery —

We're working through final numbers for the POC and one blocker from finance is understanding how Redwood will bill our very long-context calls. A few specific asks:

1) If a single call uses 60k tokens of context and streams back 6k tokens, how are pre- and post-call tokens accounted for against the minimums/quantum?
2) We plan to switch model variants mid-call (auto-fallback to smaller quantized model if latency spikes). Does that split the session for rounding?
3) We have intermittent heartbeat pings that are tiny (sub-10 token) every 30s to keep KV warm. Are those aggregated or charged per-call?
4) Any way to get predictable blended pricing for long-context-heavy routes (e.g., a single per-token rate or a context-bucket credit)?

Finance also asked whether you can provide a sample invoice row (CSV) showing how a 30-day window would reflect these patterns so they can line-item them.

Thanks — if easier, happy to hop on a quick call.

Lily
Director, Platform Integrations
AcmeHealth

Hi Lily —

Thanks for the clear list — great questions. Below is a concise breakdown and I attached a small CSV with a sample 30-day invoice that maps the scenarios you called out. Short answers up front: predictable blended pricing is possible via a context-bucket add-on and the runtime treats mid-call model fallbacks as the same session for metering (no split) unless you explicitly start a new session. Details: 

1) Long call token accounting (60k context + 6k generation): we meter request tokens (all context sent) and response tokens separately. For billing units we: 
  - Apply the per-token rate to total tokens consumed during the active session, subject to the billing quantum (default quantum = 256 tokens).
  - For very long contexts we also apply context-band normalization: the first X tokens (configurable per customer) are billed at a prioritized context rate; beyond that, tokens fall into bands with stepped discounts. This prevents extreme bills while keeping unit economics predictable.

2) Model variant fallback mid-call: our router does not break the session for metering so long as the request ID and conversation_id remain the same. That means rounding/quantum aggregation remains contiguous across model switches. If you explicitly create a new conversation/session, it will be treated as a new billing window.

3) Heartbeat / KV warm pings: by default heartbeats are charged as calls. However we offer a "heartbeat aggregation" policy for enterprise customers which collapses sub-10-token pings within a sliding window (default 5 minutes) into a single metered unit per window, and provides automatic micro-crediting for idle prefixes. We can enable an aggressive heartbeat policy for the POC.

4) Blended pricing & context-bucket option: we can propose a bundle called "Premium Context Bucket" (example: 100M context-token credits) that is consumed preferentially for long-context routes and priced at a blended per-token rate. That makes monthly spend predictable. I've sketched two options in the attached PDF (standard bucket vs. smoothing pilot with rollover).

Proposed next steps:
- I'll send a redlined example invoice CSV (attached) showing how the 60k/6k example maps to invoice lines with and without the context-bucket.
- If this looks good, Ben and Marissa can propose a pilot concession (one-time onboarding credit for KV warm-up + heartbeat aggregation enabled for 90 days).

Happy to jump on a call if useful — my calendar is open tomorrow afternoon.

Best,

Forwarding Lily's questions + my read of a sensible commercial response. Key points we should consider before we commit:

- Pilot concession: 90-day heartbeat aggregation + 5M context-token onboarding credit. Leaves us room to measure real usage and avoid giving open-ended discounts.
- Quantum rounding: default 256 is fine, but we should offer an optional 128 quantum for high-volume enterprise customers (reduces rounding waste). That should be limited to 1 route for the POC.
- Model fallback: confirm with product that mid-call quantization changes won't trigger separate kernel accounting that affects GPU allocation billing. If it does, we need to flag potential infra cost exposure.

--- Amendment: Context Bucket + Heartbeat Aggregation Pilot (90 days) ---
1) Context Bucket: Redwood will allocate a one-time context-token credit (configurable, example 5,000,000 tokens) for the POC. Credits will be consumed preferentially for tokens classified as "premium context" (long-context routes). Unused credits will not roll over after the pilot unless a subscription is signed. 2) Heartbeat Aggregation: Redwood will enable heartbeat aggregation for the POC which collapses sub-10-token requests into a single metered unit per 5-minute sliding window. Aggregation may be disabled by customer request.

3) Quantum Option: For the duration of the pilot Redwood will set billing quantum to 128 tokens on the primary route to reduce rounding overhead.

4) Measurement & Reporting: Redwood will provide per-route token breakdown and a sample invoice at the end of the pilot.

Following up with a concise commercial proposal based on your questions and our internal review. Summary of the POC offer: 

- 90-day Pilot Package (POC): includes a 5,000,000 token Premium Context Bucket (consumed first for long-context routes), Heartbeat Aggregation enabled (sub-10-token pings collapsed per 5-minute sliding window), and quantum set to 128 tokens for the primary POC route.

- Model switch behavior: session continuity preserved for metering across model fallbacks; no session split unless you explicitly create a new conversation id.
